1	# Architecture
2	
3	This repository implements a Go SDK for Pipedrive with a **stable handwritten public API** and **unexported generated OpenAPI clients**.
4	
5	## Goals
6	- **Go-idiomatic** SDK surface: services, `context.Context`, functional options, typed errors.
7	- **API coverage policy**
8	  - **API v2**: supported in full.
9	  - **API v1**: supported **only** for endpoints not yet present in v2 (“v1-legacy”).
10	- **Stability across regeneration**: users should not be exposed to generator noise.
11	- **First-class reliability**: retries and rate limiting should be painless and configurable.
12	- **Transport customization**: users can plug in their own `http.Client`/`RoundTripper` and middleware.
13	
14	## Non-goals
15	- Perfect one-to-one type parity with Pipedrive OpenAPI schemas.
16	- Exposing generated clients/types as the primary SDK surface.
17	
18	## Repository layout
19	
20	### Specs
21	- `openapi/upstream/`
22	  - `v1.yaml` — upstream snapshot of API v1 spec
23	  - `v2.yaml` — upstream snapshot of API v2 spec
24	- `openapi/derived/`
25	  - `v1-legacy.yaml` — derived from v1 by removing operations present in v2 (by `operationId`)
26	
27	### Generated code (never exported)
28	- `internal/gen/v2/` — raw OpenAPI-generated client for API v2
29	- `internal/gen/v1/` — raw OpenAPI-generated client for **v1-legacy** spec only
30	
31	### Public SDK (stable façade)
32	- `pipedrive/` — shared runtime and common types:
33	  - `Config`, auth, middleware, retry, pagination, error types, raw escape hatch
34	- `pipedrive/v2/` — handwritten API v2 façade (services + curated models)
35	- `pipedrive/v1/` — handwritten API v1-legacy façade (services + curated models)
36	
37	## Public API shape
38	
39	### Service-based client (not a “god client”)
40	Each versioned package exposes a small client with services:
41	
42	```go
43	type Client struct {
44	    Deals   *DealsService
45	    Persons *PersonsService
46	    // ...
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Each method is Go-idiomatic:
51	
52	```go
53	func (s *DealsService) Get(ctx context.Context, id DealID, opts ...GetDealOption) (*Deal, error)
54	```
55	
56	### Functional options
57	Options keep signatures stable and extensible:
58	- request options: `WithHeader(k, v)`, `WithNoRetry()`, `WithRetryPolicy(p)`
59	- list options: `WithPageSize(n)`, `WithCursor(c)`, `WithSort(...)`, `WithFields(...)`
60	
61	Options are passed down to the internal request pipeline without leaking generated types.
62	
63	## Request pipeline
64	
65	All requests flow through a single shared runtime:
66	
67	1. Build request (path params, query params, JSON body)
68	2. Apply auth + headers + user agent
69	3. Apply middleware chain (RoundTripper-based)
70	4. Execute request
71	5. Decode response
72	6. Convert errors into typed Go errors
73	7. Apply retry policy (when enabled)
74	
75	### Transport + middleware
76	Users can supply a custom `http.Client` or transport and provide middleware hooks.
77	
78	```go
79	type Middleware func(next http.RoundTripper) http.RoundTripper
80	```
81	
82	This enables logging, tracing (OpenTelemetry), metrics, or request mutation without SDK forks.
83	
84	Per-request request editors run before the transport chain. Auth providers only
85	inject `Authorization` or `x-api-token` when those headers are absent, and
86	custom middleware can still replace auth headers later in the chain.
87	
88	## Authentication
89	
90	The SDK supports:
91	- API token (`x-api-token` header)
92	- OAuth2 access token (via an auth provider callback)
93	
94	Precedence matches the Node SDK: **API token wins** if both are configured.
95	
96	Auth is modeled as an interface so users can rotate tokens:
97	
98	```go
99	type AuthProvider interface {
100	    Apply(req *http.Request) error
101	}
102	```
103	
104	## Errors
105	
106	The SDK returns errors that are useful in production:
107	- Preserve HTTP status code
108	- Preserve request ID (when present)
109	- Preserve the raw body and/or structured Pipedrive error payload
110	- Support `errors.Is/As`
111	
112	Recommended core types:
113	- `APIError` — general non-2xx responses
114	- `RateLimitError` — 429 responses with parsed rate limit headers
115	
116	## Retries and rate limiting
117	
118	Retries are first-class and configurable:
119	- default retries on: **429, 502, 503, 504**
120	- exponential backoff + jitter
121	- respect `Retry-After` when present
122	- allow per-request override: `WithNoRetry()` / `WithRetryPolicy(...)`
123	
124	The retry implementation must be observable (hooks) and must never silently hide permanent failures.
125	
126	## Pagination
127	
128	Pagination helpers should hide API quirks and feel like Go:
129	
130	### Explicit pager
131	```go
132	pager := client.Deals.ListPager(req)
133	for pager.Next(ctx) {
134	    deals := pager.Items()
135	    // ...
136	}
137	if err := pager.Err(); err != nil { ... }
138	```
139	
140	### Callback iterator
141	```go
142	err := client.Deals.ForEach(ctx, req, func(d Deal) error {
143	    return nil
144	})
145	```
146	
147	Avoid channels by default to keep cancellation semantics simple.
148	
149	## Models
150	
151	Generated models are typically not user-friendly (pointer swamp, odd names, optional wrapper types).
152	
153	Strategy:
154	- Expose curated “domain” models for common resources: `Deal`, `Person`, `Organization`, …
155	- Use typed IDs: `type DealID int64`
156	- Prefer `time.Time` only where formats are reliable; otherwise keep raw strings
157	- Preserve custom fields via a `map[string]any` or specialized type
158	- Map between façade models and generated models internally
159	
160	## Escape hatches
161	
162	Even a good SDK cannot cover every use case immediately. Provide a supported escape hatch:
163	
164	- `Raw().Do(ctx, method, path, query, body, &out)` per API version
165	
166	This avoids forcing users to import internal generated packages.
167	
168	## v1-legacy policy enforcement
169	
170	The v1 façade is intentionally limited. We enforce this mechanically:
171	- Derive `openapi/derived/v1-legacy.yaml` by removing operations whose `operationId` exists in v2.
172	- Generate `internal/gen/v1` from that derived spec.
173	
174	When an endpoint appears in v2, it disappears from v1-legacy on the next regeneration.
175	
176	## Testing strategy
177	
178	### Unit tests (default)
179	- Retry/backoff behavior and `Retry-After` handling
180	- Error decoding into `APIError`/`RateLimitError`
181	- Middleware ordering and transport customization
182	- Pagination helpers (pager/iterator) with `httptest`
183	
184	### Contract/integration tests (opt-in)
185	- Small suite hitting real endpoints behind env vars (API token/OAuth)
186	- Skipped by default so CI is safe and deterministic
187	
188	### Regeneration drift check
189	CI should fail if:
190	- `make generate` changes `internal/gen/*` without being committed
191	- wrappers stop compiling against regenerated internals
